_readme: Example domain lexicon for Meeting Scribe. Replace the entries with your own terms.
normalization.groups is rendered into the transcript lint prompt, so Claude
repairs terms in context rather than by find/replace.
See normalization._normalize_rule for which entries get substituted.
safe_auto=false marks a variant that is also a real word in the speaker's language:
the lint may substitute it from context, but nothing may do so unconditionally.

decoder_bias_rejected._verdict: Do not pass these terms to Whisper as hotwords or initial_prompt. The lint glossary is the right layer: it costs no decode budget and cannot delete speech.
decoder_bias_rejected._mechanism: Whatever the prompt occupies is taken from the budget the decoder needs to emit words, so any list large enough to bias is large enough to cost transcript.
decoder_bias_rejected._useful_facts: A model fine-tuned for one script will not switch script mid-sentence, so biasing it toward Latin terms does little.

normalization._note: variants are matched on word boundaries. safe_auto=false means the string is also a legitimate word in the speaker's language - leave it to a human or gate it on nearby context.
normalization._normalize_rule: normalize=true: the term has one canonical written form that is not in the speaker's script - proper nouns, product/service names, commands, acronyms, literal identifiers. The lint substitutes these. normalize=false: an ordinary English word used as a loanword inside the speaker's language; the native script is a correct transcription, so the lint may repair a mangled rendering but must NOT convert it to Latin.
